slot.brief: Conceptual: in the Freundlich isotherm x/m = k·P^(1/n), what happens to adsorption as pressure increases (and significance of n > 1) — statement-based recall.

stem: A gas follows the Freundlich isotherm, $\dfrac{x}{m}=kP^{1/n}$. For $n>1$, which statement is correct?
options: Adsorption is directly proportional to pressure, and the log–log plot has a slope of $1$.
Adsorption decreases with pressure, and the log–log plot has a negative slope.
Adsorption increases with pressure, and the log–log plot has a slope between $0$ and $1$.
Adsorption is independent of pressure, and the log–log plot has zero slope.

verdicts.working: Taking logs gives log(x/m) = log k + (1/n) log P. Since n > 1, the slope 1/n is between 0 and 1, so adsorption increases with pressure.

working:
$\log\dfrac{x}{m}=\log k+\dfrac{1}{n}\log P$; slope $=\dfrac{1}{n}$. For $n>1$, $0<\dfrac{1}{n}<1$, so adsorption increases with pressure with a sublinear dependence.

Independent check: Taking logs gives log(x/m) = log k + (1/n) log P. Since n > 1, the slope 1/n is between 0 and 1, so adsorption increases with pressure.
solution:
Taking logarithms of the Freundlich isotherm,
$$\log\frac{x}{m}=\log k+\frac{1}{n}\log P.$$
The log–log plot has slope $1/n$, and for $n>1$, $0<1/n<1$; hence adsorption increases with pressure sublinearly.
